b02.decision: correct and qualify first from ink
b02.evidence: The ends of celles and déduites have low terminal returns; des has its separate final s return, and the raised cercles has a final curved s below its preceding e. Retain the plurals. The shorthand is the barred reduced m/vu form, without expanding it to même. The word cone has no independently secure accent, so prefer the literal unaccented form but retain cône as a doubtful alternative. The old phrase after dessus is largely covered: d-un sommet remains a possible reading; the blind d-origine is now recorded as another possibility, although no clear g descender survives. The crossed n-est pas has a visible apostrophe, p descender and low terminal strokes, but its covered middle warrants an explicit doubt. The live Il matches the same initial form above; its looped l is not changed to Je. Disconnexe has low n/n movements and a crossing x near the end, unlike discontinue; montrera continues with additional low r/a strokes after montre. The four round vertex labels remain consistently 0/o doubtful. The first drawing retains ink visible in the crop: a parallel lower A trace, short stub below a, internal separated strokes and a gap between the left boundary and the ring; the simpler blind rendering omits these.

b03.evidence: The tiny reference letter after 1-prime is a flattened oval with a right return. It favors a but does not fully exclude 0, which is now explicit. The literal capital I, both unpunctuated l-ens forms, the insertion leader, both cancellations and the complete formula (25) remain as first read.
